summary: Viscounts of the West Kingdom, the closing entry in the West Kingdom trilogy, has players moving pieces around a shared rondel to collect resources and cards, then using deck-building-style cards to construct buildings and place bishops or knights in a king-of-the-hill contest for control of city spaces. It rewards building an efficient multi-track engine while occasionally bumping opponents off contested spots.
praised: satisfying multiple paths to victory points
polished, attractive production consistent with the trilogy
streamlined and slightly lighter than its predecessors
criticised: the rondel can feel fiddly compared to straightforward worker placement
less direct player interaction than the area-majority theme suggests
some randomness in the available card/tile offer

interaction.kind: king-of-the-hill area majority and shared rondel spaces
interaction.detail: Players displace each other's bishops and knights from contested city spaces in a king-of-the-hill mechanic and compete for the same rondel slots, but each player otherwise builds their own tableau of cards and buildings independently.

scoring.how_you_win: Send apprentices around the board to recruit more apprentices, construct buildings, and fulfill commissions for VP, while managing corruption (which costs VP unless paid off with silver); highest total VP when the apprentice supply or rounds run out wins.
